A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic collapsing problem and Test-time Embedding Adjustment (TEA) research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original embedding-drift investigations, personalization benchmark results, hyperparameter analyses, multi-concept experiments, and Anti-DreamBooth experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds OminiControl evaluations, VLM-based scores, and comparisons of adjusted and unadjusted embedding trajectories.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Equations 1–2 retain the same magnitude adjustment and SLERP rotation, applied at token level for Textual Inversion and prompt level for DreamBooth. The OminiControl evaluation introduces no documented change to TEA's procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds clock, oranges, and penguin subject cases in Table 1, extending the represented subject categories within personalization. The existing CustomConcept101, CelebA, relationship, multi-concept, and anti-personalization coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The EasyControl/ReVersion comparison in v2 Table 2 becomes an expanded comparison including OminiControl with and without TEA in v3 Table 1. Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, Custom Diffusion, and ClassDiffusion remain in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix F.2 add a GPT-4o-mini judging protocol for prompt adherence and subject identity, scored from 0–4 and normalized to percentages. This supplements the retained CLIP/DINO evaluation; the stated training settings for the existing experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 4 and 21 add direct comparisons of TEA-adjusted and unadjusted embedding norms and directions. New Figure 31 examines OminiControl's penguin/glasses failure case. Existing hyperparameter sensitivity, multi-concept, and Anti-DreamBooth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix F.2 newly specifies averaging VLM scores over 50 random generation samples for each of 16 prompts per concept/setting. This adds stochastic replication and aggregation information, without establishing increased runs for earlier experiments. Existing 50-run/100-seed analyses and plus/minus reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds EasyControl VLM scores and OminiControl results; its penguin VLM-P scores are 86.25/90.50 for OminiControl/TEA, respectively. Figures 4 and 21 add adjusted-embedding results and revise original trajectories. Figure 21's changed L2 scale is unexplained, preventing a direct cross-version numerical interpretation. Retained benchmark table entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, TEA equations, baseline optimization objectives, and distance formulations in Table 5 and Equations 1–12 are unchanged. The added VLM scoring rubric concerns empirical evaluation and introduces no new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about SCP, unconstrained embedding drift, training-free TEA, broad applicability, and partial recovery from Anti-DreamBooth corruption. The new evaluations support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 strengthens the Anti-DreamBooth interpretation: v2 describes recoverable concept traces, whereas v3 says image distortion is 'just the consequence' of extreme SCP. It also interprets the added OminiControl results as improving prompt fidelity without compromising reference fidelity. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 names the VLM judge and supplies its full system prompt, scoring anchors, output format, and aggregation details in Appendix F.2. It also reports availability of evaluation scripts in the repository. Existing hardware, learning rates, LoRA settings, and general code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tan et al. (2025), OminiControl, and positions it as another Flux-based framework evaluated with TEA. The broader related-work discussion and positioning of SCP relative to language drift and earlier personalization methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized additions and revisions to the evaluation prose, new evaluator instructions in Appendix F.2, and an updated conference header. The section hierarchy and most prose remain intact. Appendix A.2 also acquires an unresolved '(?)' citation.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves before the abstract, and Tables 1–2 exchange numbering and placement, with the expanded comparison becoming full-width. Figures 4 and 21 gain curves and revised legends; Figure 31 and a boxed VLM prompt are added. Other changes mainly involve local float placement.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2, the OminiControl tests, complementary VLM scores with an explicit rubric, and adjusted-embedding diagnostics modestly strengthen empirical support and evaluation transparency. The core method and existing benchmark results remain stable. The unexplained Figure 21 scale change and stronger Anti-DreamBooth causal wording without additional defense experiments limit the gain, but the added evidence supports a small net improvement.
